codes.subject: invocation

params.name: tool_version
params.meaning: The tool's version, as metais version prints it.

params.name: phase
params.meaning: Where the tool met the defect: parse (reading the command line), run (running the command) or output (writing its result).

codes.message: metais {tool_version} met a defect in itself ({phase}); neither the command line nor the package caused it.
codes.hint: Report the command you ran to the metais project; running it again will meet the same defect.

codes.subject: invocation

params.name: reason
params.meaning: Why the argument is refused: unknown_name (no limit has that name), malformed_value (the value is not a non-negative whole number with a unit the limit allows), or above_default (the value is higher than the limit's default, and a limit is never raised).

params.name: name
params.meaning: The limit's name, present when the argument names a limit.

params.name: default
params.meaning: The limit's default, present when the argument names a limit.

params.name: unit
params.meaning: The limit's unit, present when the argument names a limit: bytes, count or ratio.

params.name: value
params.meaning: The value asked for, in the limit's unit, present when the reason is above_default and the value is at most 2^53.

codes.message: A --limit argument is refused ({reason}); a limit can only be lowered, to a whole number no higher than its default.
codes.hint: Run `metais limits` to see every limit's name, unit and default, and give --limit NAME=VALUE with VALUE at most that default.

codes.subject: report

params.name: listed
params.meaning: How many findings the report lists before this one.

params.name: omitted
params.meaning: How many more findings were found and not listed.

codes.message: The report lists the first {listed} findings; {omitted} more were found and are counted in the summary but not listed.
codes.hint: Fix the findings listed and run the command again, or read the summary's totals by code.

codes.subject: invocation

params.name: argument
params.meaning: The 1-based position of the refused argument among the arguments after metais.

params.name: flag
params.meaning: The flag whose value is refused, written with its leading --.

params.name: reason
params.meaning: Why the value is refused: missing_value (the flag takes a value and none follows it), boolean_value (the flag takes no value and was written with =), or value_not_allowed (the value is not one the flag accepts).

params.name: allowed
params.meaning: Every value the flag accepts, present when the flag accepts a closed set of values.

codes.message: The value of {flag} at argument {argument} is refused ({reason}).
codes.hint: Give {flag} a value it accepts, as --name value or --name=value; a flag that takes no value is written alone, without =.

codes.subject: invocation
codes.message: No command was given; metais runs one command, named after any global flags.
codes.hint: Run `metais help` for the commands, and run one as metais <command>.

codes.subject: invocation

params.name: argument
params.meaning: The 1-based position, among the arguments after metais, of the flag's second occurrence.

params.name: flag
params.meaning: The flag given more than once, written with its leading --.

codes.message: {flag} is given again at argument {argument}; it may be given only once.
codes.hint: Give {flag} once: a repeated flag is refused rather than letting the last one win.

codes.subject: invocation

params.name: argument
params.meaning: The 1-based position of the refused argument among the arguments after metais.

params.name: command
params.meaning: The command that does not take the operand.

codes.message: Argument {argument} is an operand that metais {command} does not take.
codes.hint: Run `metais {command} --help` for the operands it takes; after --, every argument is an operand.

codes.subject: invocation

params.name: argument
params.meaning: The 1-based position of the refused argument among the arguments after metais.

codes.message: Argument {argument} names no metais command; a command is never abbreviated and has no alias.

codes.subject: invocation

params.name: argument
params.meaning: The 1-based position of the refused argument among the arguments after metais.

params.name: reason
params.meaning: Why the argument is refused: unknown (it names no flag accepted where it is written; before the command name only the global flags are), abbreviated (it is a prefix of a flag's name, and no flag may be abbreviated), or grouped (one-letter aliases written together, which they never are).

params.name: flag
params.meaning: The flag the argument abbreviates, or whose one-letter alias begins the group, written with its leading --; present when the reason is abbreviated or grouped.

params.name: command
params.meaning: The command whose flags the argument was read against, present when a command was named.

codes.message: Argument {argument} is not a flag this command line accepts ({reason}).
codes.hint: Run `metais help` for the global flags, or the command's --help for its own; write each flag's name in full, and each one-letter alias on its own.

codes.subject: invocation

params.name: argument
params.meaning: The 1-based position of the refused argument among the arguments after metais.

codes.message: Argument {argument} names no command or help topic.
codes.hint: Run `metais help` for the commands and the topics.
